frequency_question: How often do central fiscal/monetary authorities successfully reach a pre-announced, scaled-up volume target for a bond intervention program within a short-term window?
membership_rule: Includes: Treasury/Central Bank liquidity programs (e.g., QE, bond buybacks, YCC) where a volume target was announced and scaled. Excludes: Programs that were purely reactive to sudden market crashes without pre-defined volume goals.
provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 6 named; believed to be representative of major liquidity scaling events.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical adjustments that were not public-facing volume targets.
skeleton: Major central bank liquidity interventions since 2008 that involved scaling operations.
validity_reason: The structural behavior of central banks regarding liquidity scaling remains consistent across economic cycles.
